questions.q: In the context of Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), what is the relationship between the number of Query heads and Key/Value heads?
options: The number of KV heads is equal to the number of Q heads.
The number of KV heads is reduced by a factor of the group size compared to Q heads.
The number of KV heads is increased by a factor of the group size compared to Q heads.
The number of KV heads is always 1, regardless of the number of Q heads.
questions.answer: The number of KV heads is reduced by a factor of the group size compared to Q heads.
questions.why: The lesson states that in GQA, 'The number of KV heads is num_kv_heads = num_heads / group_size' and that 'You reduce the number of notepads (KV heads) while keeping the number of experts (Q heads) the same.'

questions.q: According to the lab results, what was the total parameter count for MHA and GQA respectively when using a group size of 2?
questions.why: The lab results section explicitly lists 'RESULT mha_total_params = 192' and 'RESULT gqa_total_params = 128'.

questions.q: Why does Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) require the head dimension to be even?
options: Because the dot product calculation requires an even number of dimensions.
Because RoPE operates on pairs of dimensions for rotation.
Because the input tensor must be square.
Because the sequence length must be even.
questions.answer: Because RoPE operates on pairs of dimensions for rotation.
questions.why: The 'Common mistakes' section states: 'RoPE requires the head dimension to be even because it operates on pairs of dimensions.'

questions.q: In the lab verification of RoPE properties, what did the equality of 'rope_relative_pos_score1' and 'rope_relative_pos_score2' prove?
options: That RoPE preserves the vector norm.
That RoPE encodes relative position, not absolute position.
That the attention score is independent of the query and key values.
questions.answer: That RoPE encodes relative position, not absolute position.
questions.why: The lab results explanation states: 'The fact that the scores are equal proves that RoPE encodes relative position, not absolute position.'
